newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica names first envoy to Cuba in 17 years.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica names first envoy to Cuba in 17 years.

text.p: Jamaica has appointed a resident ambassador to Cuba for the first time since 1980, the foreign ministry said.
Carlyle Duncan, a former trade unionist and a cabinet member in the 1970s, will take up his position soon, the ministry said in a weekend statement.
Prime Minister Percival Patterson said during a visit to Cuba in May that the Jamaican consulate in Havana would be upgraded to an embassy from Sept. 1.

Under the late Michael Manley's government in the 1970s, Jamaica developed close ties with communist Cuba to the annoyance of the United States. After Manley's election defeat in 1980 new premier Edward Seaga broke ties.
With Manley's return to power in 1989, diplomatic links were restored but the Jamaican envoy remained in Kingston.
